title: Trade-offs and the real price
blurb: Ravi has to choose between a new phone and coaching fees. Learn opportunity cost, cost per day and the real price of paying over time.
t1.title: What you give up
t1.hook: Ravi has {savings} saved. A new phone costs {phone}. A three-month coaching course costs {coaching}. He cannot afford both, so he must choose.
t1.define: **Opportunity cost** is the next best thing you give up when you choose. Every choice has one.
t1.analogy: A shop shows a phone offer. The tag shows the price in rupees. The opportunity cost is what the same rupees could have done instead.
q1.prompt: Ravi buys the phone. What is his opportunity cost?
q1.hint: It is what he gives up, not what he pays.
q1.explain: He gave up the coaching course. That is the next best use of the money.
q1.opt.a: The rupee price on the tag
q1.fb.a: The price is what you pay. The opportunity cost is the best thing you give up for it: here, the course.
q1.opt.b: The coaching course he did not take
q1.opt.c: Nothing, because he had the money
q1.fb.c: Having the money does not make a choice free. The same rupees could have paid for something else.
q2.prompt: Ravi wants both the phone and the course. How many rupees short of both is he? Type a number.
q2.hint: Add the two prices, then take away his savings.
q2.explain: {phone} plus {coaching} is {both}. Minus {savings} savings leaves {shortfall} short.
t2.title: Cost per day of use
t2.define: A big price spread over many days of use looks smaller. **Cost per day** is the price divided by the days you use the thing.
t2.steps.2: Cost per day = price ÷ days of use
q3.prompt: Ravi will use the {phone} phone for {years} years. What does it cost per day? Type a number in rupees.
q3.hint: First find the days: years times 365. Then divide the price.
q3.explain: {years} years is {days} days. {phone} divided by {days} is {perDay} a day.
q4.prompt: Phone A costs {cheapPhone} and lasts {yearsCheap} years. Phone B costs {phoneLong} and lasts {yearsLong} years. Which costs less per day?
q4.hint: Work out the cost per day for both.
q4.explain: Phone A is about {perDayCheap} a day. Phone B is about {perDayLong} a day, so B costs less per day.
q4.opt.a: Phone A, because the price is lower
q4.fb.a: A lower price does not mean lower cost per day. Divide each price by its days of use before you decide.
q4.opt.b: Phone B, because it lasts longer
t3.title: Lab: spreading the price
t3.explore: Open the lab. Change the price and how long you keep the phone. Watch the cost per day and per month.
q5.prompt: In the lab, set the price to {p5} and the years to {y5}. What is the cost per month? Type a number.
q5.hint: Read the Cost per month box.
q5.explain: {y5} years is {months5} months. {p5} divided by {months5} is {perMonth5} a month.
q6.prompt: You keep the same phone for more years. What happens to its cost per day?
q6.hint: Move the years slider and watch.
q6.explain: The price stays the same but is spread over more days, so the cost per day falls.
t4.title: Now or in parts
t4.note: A shop says: take the {phone} phone home today and pay {inst} a month for {instMonths} months. Add up every instalment and compare it with the price now.
t4.tradeoff: Paying in parts lets you have something sooner. The trade-off is that the total can be higher than the price now.
q7.prompt: In total the instalments come to more than the price now. How many extra rupees does Ravi pay? Type a number.
q7.hint: Instalment times months, then take away the price now.
q8.prompt: The shop says: only {inst} a month. Why can this still be the costlier choice?
q8.hint: Look at the total, not the monthly amount.
q8.explain: A small monthly amount hides the total. Add it all up and compare with the price now.
q8.opt.a: A small instalment means a small total
q8.fb.a: A small monthly amount hides the total. Multiply by the months and compare with the price now.
q8.opt.b: Because the total paid is more than the price now
t5.title: Challenge
t5.misconception: Many people judge a purchase by the monthly amount. The real price is the total you pay. Check how much extra you pay as a share of the price now.
q9.prompt: The extra Ravi pays is what percentage of the price now? Type a percentage.
q9.hint: Divide the extra rupees by the price now, then write it as a percentage.
glossary.plan_opportunity_cost.def: The next best thing you give up when you make a choice.
glossary.plan_cost_per_day.def: The price of something divided by the days you use it.
glossary.plan_instalment.def: One of the regular payments you make for something bought in parts.
